messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find libraries in three cities with specific facilities. We need to call the function multiple times. The function signature: public_library_find_nearby takes location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated strings? Wait: facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; That means facilities is either one of those strings or an array of strings? Actually the type says "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; So it could be a single string or an array of strings. But we need to pass multiple facilities. So we should pass an array of strings: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"] etc.

We need to call the function three times:

1. location: "New York, NY" (or "New York, NY") facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"]

2. location: "Los Angeles, CA" facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"]

3. location: "Chicago, IL" facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"]

We need to output the results. The function returns any. We need to call it. We'll do three calls. We'll use the function tool.
